mistakes.title: LH check done counterclockwise
mistakes.what: Turning the crank backward during the check.
mistakes.consequence: Chain slack moves to the wrong side and the marks appear to be off.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the crank clockwise only for this check, as the procedure says.

steps.title: Load the RH tensioner
steps.action: Compress and pin the RH tensioner plunger with the 2.5 mm stopper pin, first rack notch engaged.

mistakes.title: RH plunger pinned without notch
mistakes.what: Pinning the RH plunger without the first rack notch engaged.
mistakes.consequence: The RH chain starts under-tensioned and rattles until oil pressure builds.
mistakes.prevent: Engage the first rack notch on the RH plunger before inserting the pin.

steps.title: Time the RH sprockets
steps.action: Set the RH intake and exhaust sprockets to their marks, moving each only within its free zero-lift range.

mistakes.title: RH cam moved outside free range
mistakes.what: Swinging an RH sprocket past its free range to reach the mark.
mistakes.consequence: RH intake and exhaust valves collide and bend.
mistakes.prevent: Move each RH sprocket only within the range where it turns freely.

mistakes.title: RH timed to a free plate
mistakes.what: Using the sensor plate mark on an RH sprocket tagged as free.
mistakes.consequence: That RH camshaft ends up out of time and sets correlation codes.
mistakes.prevent: Use the housing mark on any RH sprocket tagged with a free plate.

steps.title: Hang the RH timing chain
steps.action: Fit the RH chain with the blue link on the crank mark and the pink links on the RH intake and exhaust marks, then fit the RH guide.

mistakes.title: RH chain hung to LH positions
mistakes.what: Expecting the RH marks at the clock positions used for the LH.
mistakes.consequence: The RH chain goes on with its colored links off the real RH marks.
mistakes.prevent: Use the RH mark positions from the procedure, not the LH ones.

mistakes.title: Crank moved while hanging RH chain
mistakes.what: Letting the crank rotate while fitting the RH chain.
mistakes.consequence: The LH timing that was just set moves with the crank.
mistakes.prevent: Hold the crank with its socket while the RH chain goes on.

steps.title: Release the RH tensioner
steps.action: Install the RH tensioner lever and tensioner, confirm all three RH marks, and pull the stopper pin.

mistakes.title: RH tensioner left a notch short
mistakes.what: Releasing the RH pin without squeezing the chain for the extra click.
mistakes.consequence: The RH chain is briefly slack and rattles at first start.
mistakes.prevent: Squeeze the RH chain and guides until the plunger clicks once more.

mistakes.title: Metal lever on the B1 guide
mistakes.what: Levering the RH lower guide with a bare metal tool.
mistakes.consequence: The RH lower guide is scored and wears quickly against the chain.
mistakes.prevent: Lift the guide gently with a rubber-coated plier handle.

steps.title: Rotate engine to verify timing
steps.action: Confirm all marks on both banks, then turn the crank clockwise by hand through at least two turns and check for any binding before going further.
steps.why: A timing error found now costs minutes; found after the chain cover is sealed it costs the cover.

mistakes.title: Binding forced during verification
mistakes.what: Pushing through a tight spot during the two-turn check.
mistakes.consequence: Valves bend against pistons or against each other.
mistakes.prevent: Stop at any resistance and find the cause before sealing the cover.

mistakes.title: Verified with one turn only
mistakes.what: Turning the crank only one revolution.
mistakes.consequence: A conflict that only occurs on the second revolution is missed.
mistakes.prevent: Turn the crank through at least two full revolutions by hand.

steps.title: Install injectors and fuel pipes
steps.action: Fit new O-rings, rubbers and seal rings, install each fuel pipe with its injectors and bolt it to its cam carrier.

mistakes.title: Injector O-rings reused
mistakes.what: Refitting injectors with their old O-rings and seal rings.
mistakes.consequence: Fuel seeps at the injectors onto a hot engine, which is a fire risk.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new O-rings, rubbers and seal rings to every injector.

mistakes.title: Injector O-rings fitted dry
mistakes.what: Pushing injectors in with dry O-rings.
mistakes.consequence: An O-ring rolls or tears as it goes in and leaks fuel or air.
mistakes.prevent: Wet the O-rings with clean engine oil before fitting.

steps.title: Refit the water pipes
steps.action: Connect the water pipe hoses at the oil pan upper and bolt the water pipe assemblies on.

mistakes.title: Water pipe hose clamps not set
mistakes.what: Refitting hoses without seating the clamps over the beads.
mistakes.consequence: A hose seeps coolant or blows off once the system is hot and pressurized.
mistakes.prevent: Push each hose fully on and set its clamp past the bead.

steps.title: Install the rocker covers
steps.action: Fit new spark plug tube gaskets and cover gaskets, run the sealant beads at the arches, and tighten each cover in sequence.
steps.why: The rocker covers go on before the chain cover because the chain cover seals across their ends.

mistakes.title: Plug tube gaskets reused
mistakes.what: Reusing the spark plug tube gaskets in the rocker covers.
mistakes.consequence: Oil fills the spark plug wells and causes misfires.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new spark plug tube gaskets together with the cover gaskets.

mistakes.title: Arch sealant beads skipped
mistakes.what: Fitting the cover gaskets without the sealant beads at the arches.
mistakes.consequence: Oil leaks at the arch corners of the rocker cover.
mistakes.prevent: Run the specified sealant bead at each arch before fitting the cover.

mistakes.title: Rocker cover bolts overtightened
mistakes.what: Tightening the cover bolts past spec.
mistakes.consequence: The cover distorts between bolts and leaks along its gasket.
mistakes.prevent: Torque the cover bolts to their low spec in sequence.

steps.title: Prepare the chain cover joints
steps.action: Fit new oiled O-rings at the heads, LH block half and oil pan upper, and fill any step between cam cap, carrier, head and block with liquid gasket.
steps.why: The cover seals across several separate parts, and each joint between them is a leak path.

mistakes.title: Chain cover O-rings reused
mistakes.what: Refitting the O-rings between the chain cover and the engine.
mistakes.consequence: They are one-time parts and leak oil at the cover joints.
mistakes.prevent: Fit every O-ring between the chain cover and the engine new.

mistakes.title: Steps between parts not filled
mistakes.what: Skipping the sealant fill at steps where cam cap, carrier, head and block meet.
mistakes.consequence: Oil escapes through the step under the cover bead and leaks at the front.
mistakes.prevent: Fill every step with sealant before the cover bead.

mistakes.title: Pump port O-rings damaged
mistakes.what: Fitting damaged or missing O-rings at the oil pump ports and head oil passages.
mistakes.consequence: Oil pressure to the heads drops and AVCS codes appear.
mistakes.prevent: Inspect each O-ring seat and fit new oiled O-rings.

steps.title: Seal and fit chain cover
steps.action: Run the liquid gasket bead around the cover and on its five center bosses, then slide it straight on over guide pins without touching the sprockets and tighten the bolts in sequence.
steps.why: The cover can catch the sensor plate on a cam sprocket; touching a sprocket also smears the fresh bead.

spec.note: M6 bolts 10, M8 bolts 25; 4 mm bead

steps.mistake: Swinging the cover in at an angle wipes the sealant and leaks at the cam carrier corners.

mistakes.title: Cover swung in at an angle
mistakes.what: Fitting the chain cover at an angle instead of straight on.
mistakes.consequence: The cover wipes its bead and leaks at the cam carrier corners.
mistakes.prevent: Slide it straight on over the alignment pins without touching the sprockets.

mistakes.title: Cover touches an exhaust sprocket
mistakes.what: Letting the cover brush a cam sprocket, usually an exhaust one, on the way in.
mistakes.consequence: The fresh sealant is disturbed at that spot and it leaks after reassembly.
mistakes.prevent: Use the J-51972 alignment pins, with a helper guiding the cover on.

mistakes.title: Cover bead past open time
mistakes.what: Taking too long between running the bead and tightening the cover.
mistakes.consequence: The sealant skins over before the cover is clamped and does not seal.
mistakes.prevent: Have bolts sorted and pins in before applying sealant.

mistakes.title: Center bosses left unsealed
mistakes.what: Running the perimeter bead but missing the five center bosses.
mistakes.consequence: Oil leaks out around the bolt bosses in the middle of the cover.
mistakes.prevent: Bead each center boss as well as the perimeter.

mistakes.title: Cover bolts mixed by size
mistakes.what: Putting M6 and M8 bolts in each other's holes or mixing lengths.
mistakes.consequence: A long bolt bottoms and cracks the cover or a short one does not clamp.
mistakes.prevent: Lay the bolts out in a pattern matching the cover.

mistakes.title: Excess cover sealant
mistakes.what: Running a heavy bead on the cover.
mistakes.consequence: Squeeze-out enters oil passages and blocks the AVCS feed.
mistakes.prevent: Run the cover bead at the specified size and no larger.

steps.title: Press in front crank seal
steps.action: Lightly oil the new front seal and drive it into the chain cover to just below the outer face.

spec.note: seal depth from cover end face

mistakes.title: Front seal driven too deep
mistakes.what: Driving the seal past the specified depth or unevenly.
mistakes.consequence: The lip runs on the wrong spot of the pulley boss and leaks.
mistakes.prevent: Drive the seal in square, to the depth given from the cover face.

mistakes.title: Old front seal kept
mistakes.what: Leaving the original front crank seal in the cover.
mistakes.consequence: The original seal is a one-time part and leaks soon after the rebuild.
mistakes.prevent: Always fit a new front crank seal when the cover is off.

mistakes.title: Wrong year seal prep
mistakes.what: Following the later Legacy instruction to fit the seal dry on this engine.
mistakes.consequence: The two manuals disagree, and the wrong prep can let the lip run dry or not seal.
mistakes.prevent: Follow the manual for the exact vehicle and check STIS.

steps.title: Install the AVCS solenoids
steps.action: Fit the oil control solenoids with new oiled O-rings, plus the sensor and actuator covers.

mistakes.title: OCV O-ring and backer reused
mistakes.what: Refitting the oil control valves with their old O-ring and nylon backer ring.
mistakes.consequence: Oil leaks past the valve and AVCS pressure is lost.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new O-ring and backer ring on each valve.

mistakes.title: Contaminated OCV refitted
mistakes.what: Reusing an oil control valve from an engine with sludge or AVCS codes.
mistakes.consequence: The dirty valve sticks and the AVCS codes come back.
mistakes.prevent: Replace the valve as the AVCS bulletins direct.

steps.title: Install chain cover sensors
steps.action: Install the camshaft position sensors, oil temperature sensor, oil pressure switch and the oil pump union.

mistakes.title: Oil pump union under-torqued
mistakes.what: Tightening the oil pump union by feel.
mistakes.consequence: The union weeps oil at the chain cover and pressure can drop.
mistakes.prevent: Torque the oil pump union to its specified value.

mistakes.title: Cam sensor O-ring pinched
mistakes.what: Pushing the cam position sensor in with a dry or rolled O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: Oil seeps out around the cam position sensor body.
mistakes.prevent: Lubricate the O-ring and seat the sensor straight.

steps.title: Angle-torque the crank pulley
steps.action: With a new O-ring on the pulley boss, fit the pulley on its knock pin, oil the bolt, torque it while the pulley is locked, then mark bolt and pulley and turn the bolt through the angle.
steps.why: The pulley bolt clamps the crank sprocket and boss; the angle, not the torque, sets that load.
steps.mistake: Stopping at the torque value without the angle leaves the pulley loose enough to shear its pin.

mistakes.title: Pulley bolt stopped at torque
mistakes.what: Tightening the pulley bolt to the torque value but skipping the angle.
mistakes.consequence: The pulley is left loose enough to shear its locating pin.
mistakes.prevent: Mark bolt and pulley and turn through the full angle.

mistakes.title: Pulley O-ring reused
mistakes.what: Refitting the pulley without a new O-ring on its boss.
mistakes.consequence: Oil leaks past the pulley boss at the front of the cover.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new O-ring on the pulley boss every time.

mistakes.title: Pulley not on its pin
mistakes.what: Torquing the pulley bolt with the pulley off its knock pin.
mistakes.consequence: The pulley and sprocket can slip, letting valves hit pistons.
mistakes.prevent: Seat the pulley on its pin before the bolt goes in.

mistakes.title: Pulley bolt fitted dry
mistakes.what: Installing the crank pulley bolt without oil.
mistakes.consequence: Friction is higher and the clamp load lower than designed.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the pulley bolt threads and seat before torquing.

steps.title: Fit idler and dipstick guide
steps.action: Install the idler pulley with its cover the right way round and the oil level gauge guide with a new O-ring.

mistakes.title: Dipstick guide O-ring reused
mistakes.what: Refitting the dipstick guide with its old O-ring.
mistakes.consequence: Oil seeps and unmetered air enters the crankcase.
mistakes.prevent: Fit a new O-ring to the dipstick guide before pushing it in.

mistakes.title: Idler cover fitted backward
mistakes.what: Installing the idler pulley cover the wrong way round.
mistakes.consequence: The pulley bearing is exposed to water and dirt.
mistakes.prevent: Check the idler cover orientation before torquing the pulley.

steps.title: Install water pump pulley
steps.action: Bolt the water pump pulley on while holding it with the pulley wrench.

mistakes.title: Pump pulley bolts overtightened
mistakes.what: Tightening the water pump pulley bolts past spec.
mistakes.consequence: The small pulley bolts stretch or strip the pump flange threads.
mistakes.prevent: Use a small torque wrench set to the pulley bolt value.

steps.title: Install the oil filter
steps.action: Oil the new filter's seal and turn it on by hand until it touches, then about one more turn.

spec.note: 68 mm filter; 12 N·m for the 67.4 mm filter

mistakes.title: Old filter gasket left on
mistakes.what: Leaving the old filter gasket stuck to the cover and fitting the new filter over it.
mistakes.consequence: The double gasket blows out and the engine loses its oil.
mistakes.prevent: Check the cover face is bare before fitting.
mistakes.detect: Oil spraying from the filter during priming.

mistakes.title: Filter seal dry or overtightened
mistakes.what: Spinning the filter on with a dry seal or past the specified turn.
mistakes.consequence: The seal tears or the filter is hard to remove.
mistakes.prevent: Oil the seal and turn about one turn after contact.

steps.title: Install tumble generator valves
steps.action: Fit the cylinder head plates and tumble generator valve assemblies with new gaskets.

mistakes.title: TGV gaskets reused
mistakes.what: Refitting the tumble generator valves with old gaskets.
mistakes.consequence: Air leaks cause lean codes and rough idle.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new gaskets behind every tumble generator valve.

mistakes.title: Hardware dropped in an intake port
mistakes.what: Letting a bolt or washer fall into an open port before the TGV is fitted.
mistakes.consequence: The part is drawn into the cylinder and damages the piston and valves.
mistakes.prevent: Plug the ports until each TGV goes on.

steps.title: Install harness and manifold
steps.action: Lay in the engine wiring harness, then fit the intake manifold to the tumble generator valves with new gaskets and reconnect fuel and sensor lines.

mistakes.title: Harness pinched under the manifold
mistakes.what: Laying the manifold on a misrouted harness.
mistakes.consequence: The trapped wiring chafes through and shorts.
mistakes.prevent: Route the harness into its clips before the manifold goes on.

mistakes.title: PCV or vacuum hose left off
mistakes.what: Forgetting to reconnect a PCV or vacuum hose.
mistakes.consequence: A vacuum leak and a PCV fault follow.
mistakes.prevent: Check every manifold port against the teardown photos.

mistakes.title: Manifold bolts overtightened
mistakes.what: Tightening the manifold-to-TGV bolts past spec.
mistakes.consequence: The manifold flange cracks and leaks air.
mistakes.prevent: Torque the manifold to TGV bolts to their low spec.

steps.title: Install the generator
steps.action: Bolt the generator onto its bracket and reconnect its cord stay to the chain cover.

mistakes.title: Generator terminal left loose
mistakes.what: Not tightening the generator output terminal nut.
mistakes.consequence: Arcing causes charging faults and can start a fire.
mistakes.prevent: Tighten the output terminal nut and refit its cover.

steps.title: Install tensioner and V-belt
steps.action: Fit the belt tensioner with its tab in the anti-rotation hole, then route the V-belt on clean, dry pulleys.

mistakes.title: Tensioner tab not located
mistakes.what: Fitting the belt tensioner without its tab in the anti-rotation hole.
mistakes.consequence: The tensioner turns and the belt slips.
mistakes.prevent: Seat the tab in the anti-rotation hole before tightening.

mistakes.title: Belt off a pulley groove
mistakes.what: Running the belt with a rib off a groove.
mistakes.consequence: The misaligned belt frays and can be thrown off.
mistakes.prevent: Check that the belt sits in every pulley groove before starting.

mistakes.title: Oily pulleys
mistakes.what: Fitting the belt over pulleys with oil or sealant on them.
mistakes.consequence: The belt slips and squeals on the contaminated pulleys.
mistakes.prevent: Clean the pulleys with solvent and let them dry first.

steps.title: Install plugs and coils
steps.action: Install the spark plugs and the four ignition coils.

mistakes.title: Spark plug cross-threaded
mistakes.what: Starting a plug with a wrench instead of by hand.
mistakes.consequence: The aluminum thread in the head is damaged and needs repair.
mistakes.prevent: Thread every plug in by hand first.

mistakes.title: Coil boot not seated
mistakes.what: Leaving a coil boot short of the plug.
mistakes.consequence: That cylinder misfires and sets a misfire code.
mistakes.prevent: Press each coil fully home until it sits flat.

steps.title: Fit mounts, lift off stand
steps.action: Bolt the engine mounts on, then sling the engine and remove it from the stand.

steps.title: Mate engine to transmission
steps.action: Lower the engine in, slide it straight back onto the transmission with the jack supporting the transmission, and fit the upper bellhousing bolts.

mistakes.title: Engine drawn in by bolts
mistakes.what: Pulling the engine onto the transmission with the bellhousing bolts.
mistakes.consequence: The case cracks or the converter is pushed into the pump.
mistakes.prevent: Slide until flush by hand, then fit bolts.

mistakes.title: Transmission raised too far
mistakes.what: Jacking the transmission up higher than needed to line up.
mistakes.consequence: The transmission strikes the bulkhead and tunnel.
mistakes.prevent: Raise the transmission only enough to line up the engine.

steps.title: Reconnect torque converter
steps.action: Remove the converter stopper, install the starter, then turn the crank to bolt the converter to the drive plate through the service hole and refit the plug.
steps.why: The stopper must be out before the converter can be pulled up to the drive plate.
steps.mistake: Dropping a converter bolt into the bellhousing means pulling the engine back out.

mistakes.title: Converter bolt dropped in bellhousing
mistakes.what: Losing a converter bolt into the bellhousing through the service hole.
mistakes.consequence: The engine has to be pulled back out to retrieve it.
mistakes.prevent: Hold each bolt in a magnetic tool and count them.

mistakes.title: Converter stopper left on
mistakes.what: Bolting up without removing the stopper.
mistakes.consequence: The converter cannot come forward to the drive plate.
mistakes.prevent: Remove the stopper before turning to the first converter bolt.

steps.title: Secure bolts, mounts and exhaust
steps.action: From underneath, fit the lower bellhousing bolts and the mount nuts, connect the engine ground and install the front exhaust pipe.

spec.note: mount nuts to crossmember; lower bellhousing 50 N·m

mistakes.title: Exhaust gaskets reused
mistakes.what: Fitting the front pipe with its old gaskets.
mistakes.consequence: Exhaust leaks upstream of the sensor skew the air-fuel readings.
mistakes.prevent: Fit new gaskets at both ends of the front pipe.

mistakes.title: Engine ground left off
mistakes.what: Forgetting the engine ground strap.
mistakes.consequence: No-start or current flows through other paths.
mistakes.prevent: Bolt the engine ground strap on before reconnecting the battery.

steps.title: Reconnect hoses and harness
steps.action: Reconnect fuel and evaporation lines, heater and booster hoses, the A/C line, harness connectors, radiator and intake ducting.
steps.mistake: Heater inlet and outlet hoses swapped at the engine will not heat properly and trap air.

mistakes.title: Heater hoses swapped at engine
mistakes.what: Reconnecting heater inlet and outlet to the wrong engine pipes.
mistakes.consequence: The heater gives poor output and air stays trapped.
mistakes.prevent: Match the hose tags made at removal to their pipes.

mistakes.title: Fuel connector not latched
mistakes.what: Pushing on a fuel quick connector without the click.
mistakes.consequence: It pops off under pressure and sprays fuel.
mistakes.prevent: Pull back on every fuel connector after it clicks.

mistakes.title: Booster hose left off
mistakes.what: Forgetting to reconnect the brake booster hose.
mistakes.consequence: A vacuum leak and hard brake pedal follow.
mistakes.prevent: Check the booster hose is on before the first start.

steps.title: Fill the engine oil
steps.action: Fill with 0W-20 synthetic through the filler to the F mark on the dipstick.

spec.note: total at overhaul (6.0 US qt), 0W-20 synthetic

mistakes.title: Wrong oil or additives
mistakes.what: Filling with a viscosity other than 0W-20 or adding an oil additive.
mistakes.consequence: Oil consumption rises and the AVCS can respond slowly or set codes.
mistakes.prevent: Fill with 0W-20 synthetic and add nothing to it.

mistakes.title: Level read too soon
mistakes.what: Reading the dipstick right after running.
mistakes.consequence: Oil still in the engine makes the level look low.
mistakes.prevent: Wait at least five minutes after shutdown before reading.

steps.title: Fill and bleed coolant
steps.action: Add the cooling system conditioner, fill with Subaru Super Coolant, then run the factory bleed cycle of short revving bursts, heater on full hot, until the fan cycles, topping up after each cool-down.
steps.why: The repeated rev, wait and top-up cycles work trapped air out of the engine and heater core; air left behind lets the engine overheat.

mistakes.title: Coolant bleed cut short
mistakes.what: Skipping or shortening the bleed cycle.
mistakes.consequence: Air left in the heads and heater core lets the engine overheat.
mistakes.prevent: Run the full bleed cycle, topping up after each cool-down.

mistakes.title: Wrong coolant used
mistakes.what: Filling with a generic coolant or plain water.
mistakes.consequence: The coolant does not give the corrosion protection the system was designed for.
mistakes.prevent: Use Subaru Super Coolant with the conditioner.

steps.title: Check CVTF, recharge A/C
steps.action: Check the CVT fluid level and top up if needed, then evacuate and recharge the A/C system.

mistakes.title: CVTF level not rechecked
mistakes.what: Skipping the CVT fluid check after the engine swap.
mistakes.consequence: Fluid lost during the engine swap leaves the CVT low, which damages it.
mistakes.prevent: Check and correct CVTF level as specified.

mistakes.title: A/C charged without vacuum
mistakes.what: Recharging the A/C without evacuating it.
mistakes.consequence: Moisture left in the system damages the compressor.
mistakes.prevent: Evacuate the system fully before recharging it.

steps.title: Prime the oil system
steps.action: With the fuel pump fuse removed, crank the engine in short bursts until oil pressure shows on a gauge or the warning light goes out, then refit the fuse.
steps.why: New bearings, the chain tensioners and the AVCS sprockets all need oil before the engine fires.
steps.mistake: Firing a fresh engine before oil pressure is up runs the bearings and cam journals dry.

mistakes.title: Engine fired before oil pressure
mistakes.what: Starting the fresh engine before oil pressure has come up.
mistakes.consequence: New bearings, tensioners and cam journals run without oil.
mistakes.prevent: Crank with the fuel pump fuse out until pressure shows.

mistakes.title: Cranked too long for priming
mistakes.what: Holding the starter on continuously while priming.
mistakes.consequence: The starter overheats and can fail before the prime is done.
mistakes.prevent: Crank in bursts of no more than 10 seconds.

steps.title: Start and check oil pressure
steps.action: Start the engine and confirm oil pressure with a gauge in place of the pressure switch, then look for leaks and listen for noise.

spec.note: 350 kPa or more at 6,000 rpm, oil at 80 C

mistakes.title: Ran on with low oil pressure
mistakes.what: Letting the engine run when the gauge shows low pressure.
mistakes.consequence: The new bearings are wiped within minutes.
mistakes.prevent: Shut down at once if pressure is below spec.

mistakes.title: Persistent rattle ignored
mistakes.what: Letting a rattle that continues after start-up go.
mistakes.consequence: A loose chain or a missing shim damages the timing parts or valvetrain.
mistakes.prevent: Shut down and trace any rattle that does not stop.

steps.title: Run first heat cycle
steps.action: Let the engine warm up with varied speed rather than long idling, then shut it down, let it cool and check for leaks and fluid levels.

mistakes.title: Long idle during first heat
mistakes.what: Letting the engine idle for a long time to warm up.
mistakes.consequence: The rings glaze the bores instead of bedding in.
mistakes.prevent: Vary engine speed while warming up rather than idling.

mistakes.title: Levels not rechecked after cooling
mistakes.what: Not checking oil and coolant after the first cool-down.
mistakes.consequence: Coolant drops as air purges and the engine overheats later.
mistakes.prevent: Recheck oil and coolant once the engine is fully cold.

mistakes.title: Codes not checked after first run
mistakes.what: Not scanning for codes after the first run.
mistakes.consequence: A timing or AVCS error goes unnoticed until it causes damage.
mistakes.prevent: Read codes and AVCS values after the heat cycle.

steps.title: Change oil after first run
steps.action: Drain the first oil and replace the filter after the initial heat cycle, checking the filter for metal.
steps.why: The first oil carries assembly lube and machining debris.

mistakes.title: Early oil change skipped
mistakes.what: Running the first oil and filter for a full interval.
mistakes.consequence: Machining debris and assembly lube keep circulating through the new bearings.
mistakes.prevent: Change oil and filter after the first heat cycle.

mistakes.title: First filter not cut open
mistakes.what: Throwing away the first filter unopened.
mistakes.consequence: Early metal that warns of a problem is missed.
mistakes.prevent: Cut the first filter open and look through the pleats for metal.

steps.title: Drive the 1,000-mile break-in
steps.action: For the first 1,000 miles keep the engine under 4,000 rpm, vary speed, avoid hard starts and hard braking, and check the oil level often.
steps.why: Rings seat and new parts settle during this period; Subaru notes some oil use is normal while an engine is breaking in.

mistakes.title: High rpm or heavy loads in break-in
mistakes.what: Driving hard, towing or exceeding 4,000 rpm before 1,000 miles.
mistakes.consequence: The rings seat poorly and oil consumption stays high.
mistakes.prevent: Stay under 4,000 rpm and avoid heavy loads.

mistakes.title: Oil level not checked often
mistakes.what: Not checking the dipstick during break-in.
mistakes.consequence: Early consumption runs it low before the warning lamp acts.
mistakes.prevent: Check the level often during the first 1,000 miles.

mistakes.title: Constant speed driving only
mistakes.what: Driving long stretches at one speed.
mistakes.consequence: The rings do not see the varied load they need to seat.
mistakes.prevent: Vary speed and load through the whole break-in.

mistakes.title: Oil use judged too early
mistakes.what: Declaring an oil consumption problem in the first 1,000 miles.
mistakes.consequence: A healthy rebuild is condemned or torn down for nothing.
mistakes.prevent: Wait until after break-in and run a measured test.

failureModes.title: Oil consumption past the oil control rings
failureModes.cause: Early FB25 engines used oil control rings whose surface treatment let oil past; Subaru changed the ring treatment in production and later replaced short blocks rather than rings.
failureModes.symptoms: Oil level falls well before the next change, the low oil level lamp comes on, plugs show oil fouling, and sometimes blue smoke.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit the updated ring set for the VIN (fb25-093, fb25-098), check and clock ring gaps (fb25-076, fb25-107), clean grooves and scrub honed bores (fb25-077, fb25-089), then follow the break-in (fb25-181, fb25-183).

failureModes.title: Spun rod or main bearing from low oil
failureModes.cause: Oil consumption goes unchecked between changes and the level drops far enough to starve the bearings; the low level lamp only lights once the sump is about a quart low.
failureModes.symptoms: Knock that rises with rpm, low oil pressure lamp, bearing material in the filter.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Measure and grind or replace the crank (fb25-082, fb25-091), check every clearance (fb25-081, fb25-084), clean galleries (fb25-062, fb25-060), prime before start (fb25-179) and check oil often in break-in (fb25-183).

failureModes.title: Oil seepage at cam caps and carriers
failureModes.cause: The joints between cam cap and carrier and between carrier and head rely on liquid gasket and one-time O-rings; Subaru added cleaning steps and sealer in production to cure seepage.
failureModes.symptoms: Oil wetness at the front corners of the heads, burning oil smell from the exhaust, drips on the undercover.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Clean faces without abrasives (fb25-025, fb25-062), new O-rings and correct beads at the cam caps and carriers (fb25-133, fb25-134, fb25-135, fb25-136).

failureModes.title: Front timing chain cover leaks
failureModes.cause: The long sealant bead across heads, carriers, block and pan is disturbed by poor cleaning, sprocket contact during refit, or steps left unfilled between parts.
failureModes.symptoms: Oil on the front of the engine, the lower radiator hose and the undercover.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Remove the cover with the push-off kit (fb25-024), clean with plastic tools (fb25-025), fill joint steps and fit new O-rings (fb25-157), and guide the cover on with alignment pins (fb25-158).

failureModes.title: Oil pan upper to block seepage
failureModes.cause: The sealant joint and O-rings between the oil pan upper and block weep, a leak area Subaru addressed with added sealer in production.
failureModes.symptoms: Oil along the rear of the pan-to-block seam, seen from under the car.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Separate the pan without prying the seam (fb25-053), then reseal with a correctly placed bead and new O-rings in sequence (fb25-113).

failureModes.title: AVCS slow response and over-advance codes
failureModes.cause: Contamination in a cam sprocket or oil control valve, low or dirty oil, oil additives, or excess sealant reaching the AVCS oil feed.
failureModes.symptoms: P000A to P000D, P0011, P0014, P0021 or P0024 codes, rough idle or a check engine light.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Keep sealant debris out of passages (fb25-025, fb25-062), fit new screens correctly (fb25-132), use thin beads (fb25-133, fb25-158), replace suspect sprockets and valves (fb25-071, fb25-160) and fill with the specified oil (fb25-176).

failureModes.title: AVCS oil feed blocked by a filter screen
failureModes.cause: A cam carrier filter screen is reused, pushed in too deep, or turned so its side hole misses the carrier oil passage.
failureModes.symptoms: AVCS codes soon after a carrier or timing job, and in the worst case damage from a starved AVCS sprocket.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Treat removed screens as scrap (fb25-046) and press new ones in flush with the hole lined up (fb25-132).

failureModes.title: Cam to crank correlation faults after timing work
failureModes.cause: A cam timed one tooth off, timed to a free-floating sensor plate, or a bent sensor plate after a timing chain job.
failureModes.symptoms: P0016 to P0019 codes, AVCS advance values far from the reference, poor running.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Check sensor plates before timing (fb25-026), use housing marks where needed (fb25-142, fb25-150), match the colored links (fb25-145, fb25-151) and verify by turning the engine (fb25-153).

failureModes.title: Chain rattle at start-up
failureModes.cause: A tensioner released without taking up its extra notch, worn guides, or a starved tensioner feed.
failureModes.symptoms: A brief chain rattle at cold start that may grow as guides wear.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Inspect and replace worn guides (fb25-071), fit the tensioner O-ring (fb25-146), and squeeze each chain for the extra click after pulling the pin (fb25-147, fb25-152).

failureModes.title: Cracked cam carrier after cover removal
failureModes.cause: Prying on the unsupported lower corner of a cam carrier while breaking the chain cover sealant.
failureModes.symptoms: An oil leak at a carrier corner soon after a chain cover or head job, with a visible crack in the cam cap.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Use the push-off kit and approved pry points (fb25-024), and inspect the carriers before reuse (fb25-063).

failureModes.title: Bent valves after timing chain service
failureModes.cause: A cam or the crank turned while the chains were off and a piston or the other valve was in the way.
failureModes.symptoms: Low compression on one or more cylinders and a misfire straight after a timing job.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Park the pistons and respect each cam's free range (fb25-029, fb25-032, fb25-033, fb25-138, fb25-143) and turn the engine by hand before closing up (fb25-153).

failureModes.title: PCV faults driving oil use and leaks
failureModes.cause: A sticking PCV valve or a leaking oil separator cover upsets crankcase pressure.
failureModes.symptoms: Oil in the air cleaner and throttle body, oil seepage at joints, raised oil consumption.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Fit a new oil separator cover (fb25-095), test or replace the PCV valve (fb25-117) and reconnect every PCV hose (fb25-167).

failureModes.title: Ring and bore wear from contamination
failureModes.cause: Dirt drawn through the intake or left in the engine after machining wears the top ring, bores and oil ring.
failureModes.symptoms: Rising oil use and blow-by, with fine scoring on pistons and liners when opened.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Cover intake openings (fb25-006), clean every part and passage (fb25-062) and scrub honed bores (fb25-089).

failureModes.title: No-start after short block replacement
failureModes.cause: The crank position sensor plate is fitted without being indexed on its dowel, so the crank signal is out of time.
failureModes.symptoms: The engine cranks normally but will not start.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Index the sensor plate on its dowel pin when fitting the drive plate (fb25-116).

failureModes.title: Overheating after coolant loss or poor bleed
failureModes.cause: Air left in the system after service, a weeping water pump or a sticking thermostat.
failureModes.symptoms: Temperature climbing at idle, poor heater output, coolant loss.
failureModes.rebuildAngle: Check the pump and thermostat (fb25-085), check head flatness after any overheat (fb25-064), and run the full bleed cycle (fb25-177).
